findings.reason: §3 and its unresolved decision are already implemented, so the section is a re-specification of live behaviour.
findings.text: `_declared_input_files` already charges a mere mention at a reference (zero), not at file load, and withholds the paths a negative clause governs, which is exactly §3's "a prohibition always is [a reference]"; the plan's §3 premise "today they cost the same" is false at HEAD

findings.reason: §2 and §8 are already done; the plan should be collapsed to a verification node, not an implementation node.
findings.text: `_context_refusal_detail` already reports "largest contributing files: <path> (<n> tokens)" and, when none dominates, the sentence "no repository file dominates the estimate", which is precisely §2/§8's done-when including its small-contribution case

findings.reason: if an explicit opt-out is wanted it should generalise the existing provenance field, so the plan names that field and extends it.
findings.text: §4's "anchor opt-out" overlaps the existing `provenance` mechanism (`"granted"` vs `"declared"`), where a granted path is already un-counted (line 3158 `chargeable = provenance == "declared"`); the plan proposes a new opt-out surface beside a working exemption

findings.reason: the honest change is to extend the run record and its promotion path, not to add a second marker store.
findings.text: the reduced-brief marker proposes a new recorded fact but does not name the run/ledger record it extends, nor why the refusal/accept pair cannot be joined from the existing dry-run payload to produce it

findings.reason: the section should extend the existing exemption rather than add one.
findings.text: the anchor opt-out duplicates the `provenance`/`granted_paths` exemption in `_context_file_inputs` without citing it

findings.reason: §7's done-when ("two nodes do NOT conflict on the directory, but DO conflict on the same filename") is achieved by the per-node fragment the code already grants; the section contradicts its owner and should instead extend `_landing_fragment_paths`.
findings.text: `_shared_landing_paths` already computes `docs/figures/<plan>/` and its docstring states these shared grant paths "are no longer granted by default, because a grant every node holds is exactly the merge conflict"; the default grant is instead the per-node fragment `docs/figures/<plan>/<node-id>/` in `_landing_fragment_paths` (dispatch.py:2006-2035, granted at 2081) — §7 asks to re-introduce the shared directory the owner deliberately retired

findings.reason: §7 is solving a hazard the current grant already prevents for fragment-based nodes.
findings.text: `_context_file_inputs` grants the per-node fragment via `_landing_fragment_paths`, so a node already receives a writable figures scope without asking; §7's premise that a doc-producing node "writes outside its fence" is false for the fragment path

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the only novel sections add a ledger marker (§5) and an opt-out flag (§4); neither hides substantial behaviour behind a smaller interface, and both are thin additions to existing records rather than deep modules.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §7 proposes granting every node the plan-wide figures directory, duplicating a decision the code already made and reversed.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §2/§3/§8 add no surface because they already exist, but §4 adds a CLI option and §5 adds a record field without naming what either retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's premise is contradicted by `reckon/crew/routing.py`; it cites the estimator file but not the functions that already implement §2/§3/§8.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §5's reduced-brief marker and §4's opt-out are thin wrappers over existing mechanisms with no statement of why the mechanism cannot be extended.
